$comment: AI technical pre-review of kernel-rules.cpu-memory.json inventoryVersion 1. This file RECORDS the review; it certifies nothing. Human SME sign-off happens only in kernel-rules.cpu-memory.json smeGate.

dispositions.reason: Sound textbook abstraction for an explicitly non-hashed set-associative cache. Existing caveat about real hashed/sliced caches is sufficient.
Correct LRU model. Real processors frequently use approximations (pseudo-LRU) rather than true LRU; the inventory already states that limitation.
For the stated cyclic >associativity one-set pattern under LRU the mechanism is sound: conflict misses arise precisely because too many active lines compete for one set.
Capacity pressure is real; but 'evenly spread misses' and especially 'spread misses + low reuse => capacity' are properties of these recipes, not a generally safe diagnostic law.
dispositions.appliedFix: claim/realWorldBasis rewritten: spread pattern is a generated-recipe signature; heuristic explicitly labelled a model separator with real-world counterexamples (poor spatial locality also spreads).

dispositions.reason: Conceptual compulsory miss is sound, but 'first touch => observed miss' can be defeated by hardware prefetch. Model must distinguish conceptual cold miss from what a demand-miss counter shows.
dispositions.appliedFix: claim now distinguishes conceptual cold miss from observed demand-miss rate and points at prefetch interaction.

dispositions.reason: 'Nearly every access misses' needs conditions: sufficiently fresh/large stream, no useful reuse. Not true for every strided workload.
dispositions.appliedFix: conditions added to claim; gap-pattern bins re-labelled as solver-separability boundaries.

dispositions.reason: Underlying reasoning sound: reuse can exist while reuse distance exceeds cache retention. Flat-cache simplification already disclosed.
Direction useful pedagogically, but 'useful if demanded later' ignores timeliness, adaptation and pollution. Learner must not absorb useful-fraction thresholds as hardware heuristics.
dispositions.appliedFix: realWorldBasis expanded: thresholds labelled model-relative separators; timeliness/adaptation/pollution named as unmodelled.

dispositions.reason: Keep the fiction if clearly surfaced as a model device, but 'more useful prefetch => faster' is too strong: bandwidth, pollution, MLP and queue pressure can reverse it.
dispositions.appliedFix: diagnosticHeuristicTrained weakened to conditional form; reversal conditions named in realWorldBasis.

dispositions.reason: Flat constants fine as internal toy cost model; 'fewer misses => proportionally faster' is not safe — misses differ in cost and overlap (cf. Intel Optimization Reference Manual on multi-level behaviour).
dispositions.appliedFix: diagnosticHeuristicTrained restricted to ratio reasoning within one world's baseline comparison; absolute-cycle prohibition kept.

dispositions.reason: Ownership-transfer direction is sound and line contention is exactly what perf c2c exposes; but saying the word-level ledger 'mirrors' HITM attribution is too strong — HITM/c2c is cache-line oriented; this synthetic ledger is not literal protocol evidence.
dispositions.appliedFix: realWorldBasis rewritten: ledger is an attribution abstraction over line-granular coherency traffic; c2c comparison softened to analogy.

dispositions.reason: Same-address vs different-address writes within one line is a useful distinction, but '>80%' must be labelled purely as a generated-world separator; no universal 80% boundary exists.
dispositions.appliedFix: threshold explicitly labelled a model separator; clean-mode caveat strengthened.

dispositions.reason: Simulating L1 and L2 independently over the SAME demand stream and presenting them as hierarchy statistics is causally misleading: real lower-level traffic is conditional on higher-level misses/evictions. Either simulate hierarchically or relabel as counterfactual caches.
dispositions.actionTaken: SUBSTANTIVE CODE RETUNE IMPLEMENTED: runHierarchy/analyze now perform a true conditional walk — L2 receives only L1 demand misses. Verified: mixed workload shows conditional L2 accesses = L1 miss count (224) vs independent run (2240). Residual disclosed simplification: evicted-line back-invalidation not forwarded.

dispositions.reason: Compare-against-known-good lesson is excellent, but learner-facing material must identify the twin as a lab construct, not imply production baselines normally look like this.
dispositions.appliedFix: realWorldBasis/diagnosticHeuristicTrained updated; learner-facing disclosure obligation recorded for UI work.

dispositions.reason: Correct abstraction for successive observation windows over continuous execution; arbitrary window size and ideal phase alignment harmless if disclosed.

principlesNoted: The inventory did its job: risky assumptions were visible next to their caveats; no hidden fiction had to be reverse-engineered.

The dangerous rules are the plausible compressed heuristics, not the declared fictions: spread-misses=>capacity, first-touch=>measured-miss, useful-prefetch=>faster, fewer-misses=>proportionally-faster, 80%-same-word=>true-sharing, independent-size-runs=>hierarchy.
